``` python
def foo():
    """foo"""

def bar():
    pass

fo
ba
```

issue.body:
Maybe Im understanding remote plugins incorrectly, but I tried something like:
```
    @neovim.command('SleepEcho', range='', nargs='*', sync=False)
    def command_handler(self, args, range):
        time.sleep(5)
        self.vim.command('redraw | echo "Woke up"')
```

I was expecting to be able to use nvim while the process was sleeping (or doing a long computation), but what Im experiencing is that the screen does not reflect any of the commands or text Im editing while the command is running the sleep, and when returning back from the sleep, all those modifications are applied. Am I missing something?

Thanks,
A

body:
Is this still an issue/confirmed to be a nvim issue? Bad behavior in rplugins can cause lock-ups, it is not necessarily a nvim bug.

As for the `print('foo')` issue, I believe it was covered by https://github.com/neovim/pynvim/pull/377

> Neovim should be able to abort the `rpcrequest` always

Does ctrl-c always abort rpcrequest()? If not, that seems like reason to keep this open.
